```{r}
query_seq <- "LVQPGGSLRLSCATSGRDFSTSPMAWYRQAPGKEREWVAGGIETLRIDYADSVKDRFTISRDRAKNTMYLQMNSLKPEDPAVDYCRSDSYWGRGTQVTVSS"

root_dir <- "~/Downloads/"
input_file <- "XMY-H5_query_results29Jul24.csv"
database_file <- "query_back/E_S61_db-pass.tsv"
# output_file <-"E_S6_min_threshold_clone-pass.csv"

tmp <- read.csv(paste0(root_dir, input_file), header = T, stringsAsFactors = F)

tmp <- tmp[grepl(".fasta", tmp$file),]
tmp$file <- gsub("_db-pass.fasta", "", tmp$file)

colnames(tmp)[1] <- "query_id"
colnames(tmp)[2] <- "sequence_id"
```

## Load in VHH data

```{r}
results <- read.csv(paste0(root_dir, database_file), sep = '\t', header = T, stringsAsFactors = F)

# Translate VHHs
results$VHH <- fixed_translate_DNA(results$sequence_alignment)
results$VHH <- substr(results$VHH, 11, nchar(results$VHH))

results <- unproductive(results)
```

### Boxplot of Query Results

```{r}
boxplot(tmp$fident ~ tmp$file, las = 3, ylim = c(0, 1), main = "Homology of 300 Located Target Sequences per Illumina Run\n Query Seq: XMY-H5", xlab = "Experiment ID", ylab = "Identity")
```

## Merge query data to genetic data

```{r}
results <- merge(tmp[tmp$file == "E_S61",], 
                 results, 
                 by = "sequence_id", 
                 all.x = TRUE)
```

## Join to Global Set on VHH

```{r}
dat <- read.csv("~/Downloads/GS_NGO1549_d2VHH_09Jul24_min_threshold_clone-pass.csv", header = T, stringsAsFactors = F)

# Cleanup
dat$VHH <- substr(dat$VHH, 11, nchar(dat$VHH))
dat <- unproductive(dat)

# We only need the observations that are already in our current results
dat <- dat[which(dat$VHH %in% results$VHH),]
```


```{r}
dat <- merge(dat[,c("VHH", "junction", "junction_aa", "v_call", "d_call", "j_call","dist_nearest","clone_id")], 
              results, 
              by = c("VHH", "junction", "junction_aa", "v_call", "d_call", "j_call"))

dat <- dat[!duplicated(dat),]
```

```{r}
table(dat$junction_aa)
```

## Format Clones

Before trees can be built, data must be formatted into a data table of AIRR clone objects. This is accomplished using the formatClones function. This function will:

1. Change non-nucleotide characters to N characters.

2. By default, collapse sequences that are either identical or differ only by ambiguous characters.

3. Sequences will not be collapsed if they differ by columns specified in the traits option, or if the `collapse` option is set to `FALSE`.

4. Include data columns specified by `num_fields` or `text_fields`.

5. Remove uninformative sequence sites in which all sequences have N characters.

```{r}
# Process example data keeping samples from different times
# distinct, adding duplicate_count among collapsed sequences,
# and show the sample_id within each clone in the tibble.
clones <- formatClones(results, traits=c("junction_aa", "VHH"),
                       num_fields=c("duplicate_count"))#,
    # num_fields=c("duplicate_count"), 
    #columns=c("f"))

print(clones)
```


```{r}
# Add tree info
clones <- getTrees(clones, nproc=4)
```

```{r}
# Pull from query results only those CDR3's of the same length
tmp <- results[nchar(results$junction_aa) == nchar("CNADFRYW"),]
tmp <- tmp[!grepl("\\*", tmp$junction_aa),]
```

```{r}
# Dendrogram VHHs
strings <- tmp$VHH

CDR3s <- trim_CDR3(tmp$junction_aa)

# Compute the distance matrix
dist_matrix <- stringdistmatrix(strings, method = "lv")

# Perform hierarchical clustering
cluster_tree <- hclust(as.dist(dist_matrix), method = "complete")

# test <- tmp[cluster_tree$order,]

main_title <- paste("Cluster Dendrogram of NADFRY CDR3 Family Data\nDemand >= ", 2," VHHs, Distance Metric: Levenshtein", sep = '')

par(family = "Courier", cex = 1)#0.75)#0.55)

# Plot the dendrogram with labels
plot(cluster_tree, 
     main = main_title, 
     xlab = "Overall VHH Count-Mode CDR3", sub = NULL, 
          labels = CDR3s,#[cluster_tree$order]), 
     ylab = "Distance (Levenshtein)", 
     cex = 1)#0.75)#0.55)

```


```{r}
test <- tmp[,c("junction_aa","VHH", "clone_id", "duplicate_count")]
test <- test[order(test$duplicate_count, decreasing = T),]
test$junction_aa <- trim_CDR3(test$junction_aa)
test <- test[test$duplicate_count >= 2,]
test$dist_from_query <- as.numeric(100 - (adist(query_seq, test$VHH)/nchar(query_seq)*100))
test <- test[order(test$dist_from_query, decreasing = T),]

```


```
write.csv(test, file = "~/Downloads/Query_data.csv", row.names = F)
```

# Clonal Consensus Cluster Dendrograms (Non-Hierarchical)

35in seems to work for width with portrait orientation

Note: Complete Linkage: Merges clusters based on the maximum pairwise dissimilarity.

```{r}
# Install and load necessary packages
#install.packages("stringdist")
library(stringdist)

strings <- df[df$f == "19_VecF1_R3_S19_min_threshold_clone-pass.tsv",]$consensus_sequence

strings <- strings[!duplicated(strings)]

# strings <- strings[nchar(strings) < 20]

# Compute the distance matrix using Jaccard distance
dist_matrix <- stringdistmatrix(strings, method = "jaccard")

# Perform hierarchical clustering
cluster_tree <- hclust(as.dist(dist_matrix), method = "complete")

# Plot the dendrogram with labels
plot(cluster_tree, main = "Cluster Dendrogram of 19_VecF1_R3_S19\nDistance Metric: Jaccard Similarity", xlab = "Clonal Family Consensus CDR3s", sub = NULL, labels = strings, ylab = "Distance (Jaccard Similarity)")
```
